verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The phone rings twice in an empty house and then stops.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
dust settles back
onto the sunlit table—
no one to notice

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
a moth finds the lamp
still warm from a hand that left
before the light did

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
footsteps on the porch
turn away before knocking—
the mail waits all day

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
rain begins softly
on a note left by the door—
ink already runs

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
someone folds the note
before the words can be read
pockets it like rain

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the porch light clicks off
somewhere, a kettle forgets
the water it holds

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
steam fogs the window
someone writes a name in it
then wipes it clean, waits

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the glass stays empty
where the name was breathed and gone—
morning takes the rest

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
a bus pulls away
someone waves at no one now
the road keeps the dust

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the timetable flaps
in wind that no one reads twice
noon forgets its hour

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
a coin drops in the slot
the phone booth glass holds our breath
no one dials home

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the streetlight blinks on
alone above the crossing
shadows learn to wait

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
an empty bench warms
where the sun forgot to leave
someone's shape still there

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
dust settles slow
on tracks no train remembers
evening keeps the hush

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
a moth taps the glass
looking for the light it lost
we call this waiting too
